reason: Use Tier 2: separate context and candidate item representations. The uniform preference branch produced the best observed HR@10 of 0.5375, while subsequent recency and hard-negative changes declined to 0.4838; this motivates a representation change rather than further sampling or weighting adjustments. Shared embeddings must simultaneously encode history preferences and distinguish candidate items, creating potentially conflicting gradients; untied embeddings directly test this hypothesis without repeating earlier experiments.

Preserve SASRec's existing constructor arguments and forward(self, seq), ranking_loss(self, seq, pos, negative), and predict(self, seq, candidates) signatures, adding only an optional trailing untied_output=True configuration argument. Keep the current preference pooling, gate, loss weighting, 144-negative sampler, mining procedure, optimizer, and hyperparameters unchanged so this experiment isolates embedding-role separation.
